newsitem.title: USA: Ill. tollway auth to have budget by Dec 15 - judge.
newsitem.headline: Ill. tollway auth to have budget by Dec 15 - judge.

text.p: A Cook County Ciruit Judge on Wednesday asked the Illinois State Toll Highway Authority to develop a budget by December 15 in order to comply with state law.
Judge Stephen Schiller said "the sunset date" is to give Illinois lawmakers an opportunity to address his previous ruling finding the Toll Highway Authority's budget process unconstitutional.
Schiller ruled last week that the authority's decades old practice of making continuing appropriations without oversight of the governor or General Assembly violated the state constitution.
Toll payers challenging the system had sought Wednesday to enjoin the authority from most expenditures excluding debt service, police protection and emergency road repairs.
While not a complete victory for the plaintiffs, Schiller's decision "in essence" gives them what they sought and only delays enforcement, attorney Lee Schwartz said.
The General Assembly is scheduled to meet in a veto session from mid-October to mid-November and Schiller's decision also gives the authority time to seek an Illinois Supreme Court review.

"If the Illinois General Assembly does not pass an appropriation come the veto session it appears that there will be a sunset as described by the court of any expenditures by the Toll Highway Authority," Schwartz said.

Attorney George Sotos, representing the Toll Highway Authority as a special state attorney general, promised to appeal Schiller's ruling and contended Wednesday that enjoining most expenditures would have a catastrophic effect on the authority.
Delaying enforcement of the ruling will allow the Toll Authority to continue to operate in the meantime, Sotos said.
"The motoring public won't be affected and there won't be any interruption or disturbance of the effectiveness of the Toll Authority," Sotos said.
Sotos contended before Schiller that the authority would need to make more than interest payments on outstanding debt to satisfy its agreements with bondholders.
Schiller directed the plaintiffs to prepare an order including the sunset language for submission to him Thursday.
